tour.name: Chiang Mai Private Tour: Doi Suthep, the Old City Temples & a Khao Soi Lunch
tour.subtitle: A private day in the capital of the old Lanna kingdom with a licensed guide and car: the golden mountain temple of Wat Phra That Doi Suthep, the forest temple of Wat Umong, Wat Chedi Luang and Wat Phra Singh in the walled old city, a khao soi lunch and a conversation with a monk.

tour.overview:
Chiang Mai was founded in 1296 by King Mangrai as the capital of Lanna, the 'kingdom of a million rice fields', which ruled northern Thailand for two centuries and kept its own language, script and art. Its square old city, still surrounded by a moat and fragments of brick walls, holds more than thirty temples, and above it the forested mountain of Doi Suthep is crowned by the most sacred temple of the north.

This private day shows the temples and culture of Chiang Mai with a licensed guide and a car. You drive up to Wat Phra That Doi Suthep in the cool of the morning, visit the forest temple of Wat Umong, eat khao soi for lunch, explore the great temples of the old city, and meet a monk to learn about daily life in a monastery.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 7 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Chiang Mai
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; 306 steps at Doi Suthep (a funicular is available)

WHAT YOU SEE
• Wat Phra That Doi Suthep.
• Wat Umong.
• Wat Chedi Luang and the city pillar.
• Wat Phra Singh.
• The moat and gates of the old city.

WHY THIS WORKS
We reach Doi Suthep early, before the heat and the crowds, and spend the hottest hours in the shade of temple halls and over lunch.

WHO IT SUITS
First-time visitors to northern Thailand, families and anyone interested in Buddhism.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you want nature and animals, choose our ethical elephant sanctuary day.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Shoulders and knees must be covered in all temples; shoes are removed in the halls. On Sundays the Walking Street market fills the old city in the evening and can be added.

days.name: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep, Wat Umong, a khao soi lunch, Wat Chedi Luang, Wat Phra Singh and a monk chat
days.description:
What to expect: the sacred mountain and the temples of the Lanna capital, with a licensed guide, private car, temple fees and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 7:30 and drive up the winding road through the forest to Wat Phra That Doi Suthep, 1,000 metres above sea level. According to legend, a white elephant carrying a relic of the Buddha climbed the mountain in the 14th century, trumpeted three times and died on this spot, where the king built the temple. You climb the 306 steps of the staircase flanked by two long naga serpents, or take the funicular, to the terrace where the gilded chedi shines among bells, umbrellas and statues, and look out over Chiang Mai and the plain.

On the way down you stop at Wat Umong, a peaceful forest temple founded around 1300, where monks meditated in brick tunnels dug into a hillside, still decorated with traces of old murals. Lunch is khao soi, the signature dish of the north: egg noodles in a rich coconut curry broth, topped with crispy noodles and served with pickled mustard greens, shallots and lime.

In the afternoon you enter the old city through one of its gates. At Wat Chedi Luang stands a massive brick chedi built in the 15th century, once 80 metres tall, partly destroyed by an earthquake in 1545; it housed the Emerald Buddha for some eighty years. Here you sit down for a 'monk chat', a friendly conversation in which young monks practise their English and answer your questions about meditation, food and monastic life. You end at Wat Phra Singh, the most revered temple of the city, whose small Lai Kham chapel is decorated with 19th-century murals of Lanna daily life and a gilded Buddha. You are back at your hotel at about 14:30, or on a Sunday we can take you to the Walking Street market.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:30 – Pick-up at your hotel.
08:15 – Wat Phra That Doi Suthep.
10:00 – Wat Umong.
11:30 – Khao soi lunch.
12:45 – Wat Chedi Luang and monk chat.
13:45 – Wat Phra Singh.
14:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Women must not touch monks or hand them objects directly.
• A Thai cooking class or the Sunday Walking Street can be added.
• An evening Khantoke dinner with Lanna dances can be booked.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, temple fees and funicular, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks with lunch, donations, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Do we have to climb the 306 steps?
faq.answer: No. A funicular goes up to the temple terrace; the steps are optional and beautiful.

faq.question: Are the entrance fees included?
faq.answer: Yes, all temple fees and the Doi Suthep funicular.

faq.question: What is a monk chat?
faq.answer: An informal conversation with monks at Wat Chedi Luang, who welcome visitors' questions about Buddhism and monastic life while practising their English.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, khao soi or another northern Thai dish. Vegetarian and other diets are easy to arrange.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children enjoy the naga staircase, the tunnels and the monks. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. The funicular serves Doi Suthep, and the old city temples are on flat ground. Shoes are removed at the hall entrances.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Clothes covering shoulders and knees, and shoes easy to remove. A light layer for the mountain in the cool season.

faq.question: Can we add a cooking class?
faq.answer: Yes. A half-day Thai cooking class with a market visit is a Chiang Mai favourite.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops at silk, silver or umbrella factories unless you ask.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Thailand but never required.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: November to February is cool and dry. March and April can be smoky from crop burning; the rainy season is green and quieter.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
